Separately, setup_wizard.py never sets fallback_to_cloud=False when the user picks local_only during onboarding -- it only writes `mode` (fallback_to_cloud defaults True, core/__init__.py:1706, regardless of chosen mode). routes/chat.py DOES have a 'LOCAL ONLY MEANS LOCAL ONLY' refusal (941-987), but it only fires when the router already chose local and the live Ollama call then throws mid-request -- it never runs when the router decided cloud up front, which is exactly this case. tests/unit/test_model_router.py:597-604 documents this as known/tolerated (asserts only 'provider' in result, never provider=='local'), not as intentionally-correct.
queue_reason: URGENT but genuinely not a one-line fix: closing this gap needs coordinated changes across setup_wizard.py (actually set fallback_to_cloud=False for local_only), model_router.py (make 2 of 3 Ollama-unavailable branches respect the flag, which they currently ignore entirely), AND a decision about what local_only should DO when it truly cannot reach any local model with cloud forbidden -- refuse with a clear error (matching chat.py's existing mid-request refusal pattern), queue the turn, or something else. That last part is a real product/UX decision on the app's most safety-critical default, not a mechanical wire-up, and getting the failure-mode shape wrong risks crashing callers that assume a local result always has a model. Flagging as the single highest-priority item in this ledger for Stephen's morning review.

seam: onboarding copy vs vault passphrase storage

evidence: services/vault_passphrase.py's own docstring: 'the passphrase is written to BOTH the keychain and a DPAPI-wrapped file, and either one alone is enough to open the vault.' store() unconditionally writes ~/.friday/security/vault-passphrase.dpapi on Windows in addition to the keychain -- a real file a user can open (in a hex editor, Get-Content, etc); its bytes are just DPAPI ciphertext, unreadable as plaintext without CryptUnprotectData under the same Windows account. fix_note: A dedicated verifier traced every retry-with-provider-switch path (worker adapters, compute_client, scheduler retries, orchestrator, _generate_agent's cloud/local ladder, chat.py's inline fallback + redispatch closures) at the object-identity level and confirmed none of them reuse a caller-supplied messages/convo list across a provider switch -- each rebuilds a fresh plain {role,content} copy. So this gap could not be triggered by any code that exists today. Fixed anyway per the verifier's own recommendation: one accidental refactor (a future _call_ollama/_call_openai optimization that reuses the passed-in list directly) would make it live, and the fix mirrors an existing, already-battle-tested pattern (_gate_tool_use) rather than inventing new policy.
evidence: egress_gate.py's coverage list only names the Anthropic block shape (system, messages[].content, content[].tool_result, content[].tool_use.input). The OpenAI-compatible wire shape's tool_calls[].function.arguments field (used by _oai_agentic_loop, agent.py:6724-6878, for every OpenAI-compatible provider including cloud OpenAI/OpenRouter/Groq) has zero handling anywhere in egress_gate.py -- confirmed by grep, zero matches for 'tool_calls'. _gate_messages (836-879) and _scrub_all (1303-1334) both only recurse into content/text/system/prompt/context keys. This is the same defect class ('gating the content is not gating the decision to send', already documented 3x in KNOWN_ISSUES.md) in a 4th, previously-undocumented shape. HOWEVER the finder traced the two obvious cross-call vectors (model_router.py:646-649/950-953's message normalization drops tool_calls on rebuild; routes/chat.py:1562-1568's cross-turn history flattening also drops it) and both incidentally close the door for the /api/chat/send path today. The one unverified path: does any worker/orchestrator/sub-agent retry (services/worker_adapters/, compute_client.py, scheduler.py) reconstruct a messages list that preserves a tool_calls-bearing turn from one provider's raw response and hand it to a DIFFERENT provider mid-task -- the same shape as the already-fixed Anthropic tool_use cross-provider leak? RESOLVED: verifier confirmed CONFIRMED UNREACHABLE (see fix_note).

claim: THREAT_MODEL/Settings budget controls actually protect against unbounded spend; cost_meter tracks all real cloud spend
evidence: (a) cost_budget is explicitly alert-only by design comment ('v1 is alert-only -- Friday is never silently blocked from working', core/__init__.py:1533-1542) and daily_enabled/monthly_enabled default False -- this is documented intentional design, not a code/claim mismatch, but it is the exact unaddressed root cause of the historical $1,189.76-vs-$50 incident, still fully reproducible today. (b) budget_enforcer.reserve_budget() IS fail-closed but only gates orchestrator/goals worker tasks in a synthetic milli-Positron unit never reconciled to USD, and orchestrator.py:219-220 wraps the call in a bare except:pass with comment '# budget enforcement is best-effort' -- explicitly intentional fail-open-on-error, not a bug. (c) Gemini TTS (voice_engine.py _synthesize_tts_wav_gemini) and the Gemini Live voice websocket (routes/voice.py) make real, billed Gemini calls with ZERO cost_meter integration -- no usage capture anywhere in either file -- despite cost_meter.PRICING already having entries for exactly those models, showing clear original intent to track them. This third part is the highest-priority sub-item: real spend is currently invisible to both the dashboard and the (non-blocking) alert system.
queue_reason: (a) and (b) are explicitly-commented intentional design choices -- changing them is a real policy call about how aggressively Friday should ever refuse to work, squarely 'changes what the product does.' (c) is the closest to an unambiguous fix (wire cost_meter.meter() at the two Gemini voice call sites) but computing real USD cost from Gemini TTS/Live's billing model (likely per-second-of-audio, not per-token) needs research into the actual API response shape that this run did not have time to do carefully for a real-money accounting path -- queued rather than risking a wrong number landing unattended overnight.
